Now speaking

Morning, George — Wednesday, the fifth of August.

Good news first: that furnace over Athens isn't going anywhere, but the fire danger's eased off the extreme rating back down to plain high, so today's a notch less white-knuckle than the weekend.

Abroad, the Iran story's finally showing real movement — Qatar's now brokering, and there's an actual draft deal doing the rounds.

— personal items —

Let's go abroad, and it's still Iran out front.

After weeks of strikes and false starts, this is the closest thing to progress yet: Qatar says talks are in "very progressive stages," with drafts of an agreement actually circulating, though Washington and Tehran still aren't talking face to face.

One Iranian negotiator put the goal bluntly — a one-to-three-month arrangement where Iran runs security and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and stays, in his words, dominant.

Nothing's signed, but the mood has clearly shifted.

Meanwhile in Ukraine, another grim overnight: Russian strikes killed three people in a residential block in Sumy and one more in a drone attack on Mykolaiv, with seven wounded.

Ukraine says it shot down a hundred and seventeen of a hundred and thirty-six incoming drones — and it's cutting both ways, with a strike near Moscow injuring ten.

And a genuinely cool one from the science desk: researchers built a hydrogen turbine that makes its own pressure using controlled detonation waves instead of a big mechanical compressor, and used it to make electricity.

If it scales, it's a lighter, simpler way to burn clean hydrogen for power.

Over to AI, and it's another quiet one — no new flagship's shipped, so Claude's Opus 5 from a couple of weeks back still tops the intelligence charts.

Google's pushed out a smaller Gemini Flash update, but its proper top-tier model still hasn't landed, so treat any launch buzz as rumour.

The thing worth your time as an app builder hasn't changed: those cheap open-weight coding models are the real story right now.

Weather here in Athens: more of the same furnace.

Mid-twenties first thing, up to around thirty-five this afternoon under clear skies, easing to the high twenties by evening.

No rain anywhere, and that gusty northerly Meltemi's still blowing — which is exactly what's kept the fires going.

Sun goes down just before half past eight.

Staying home a second: that big wildfire west of Athens is still burning, but the winds have calmed enough that the water-bombers and helicopters are flying freely again after the week's tragedies.

Civil protection's dropped Attica to high risk rather than extreme — better, not over.

So if you're heading out that way, still give the fire zones a wide berth.

Onto your world.

— personal items —

With another mid-thirties day and this bone-dry air, keep the water coming all day — genuinely more than you think you need, especially around any climbing.

A quick one for the backlog: on Epic, OTXO — that slick John-Wick-style top-down shooter — plus Sol Cesto are only free to keep through tomorrow, so grab them today if you want them.

After that it rolls to Beacon Pines and the co-op puzzler We Were Here Together.

And to send you off — word of the day is "crimp": a climbing grip where you bend your fingers hard over a tiny edge, fingertips only, as in "the whole route came down to one brutal crimp."

And a fact to chew on: an octopus has three hearts and blue blood — two pump to the gills, one to the body, and it runs on copper, not iron.

So — another scorching, high-alert Wednesday, but a calmer one than the weekend: hydrate hard, dodge the fire zones, and grab those free games before they're gone.
